title: Sarah Salois
text:
A little more about me …
Marine Ecologist        Fisheries Biologist   


My Research Pillars:

Cooperative Research: Building strong, collaborative partnerships between the fishing industry and science to improve trust and management outcomes.
Integrated Ocean Data: Integrating a variety of data including in-situ subsurface data, satellite data, and oceanographic model outputs to better understand our marine ecosystems.
Data Accessibility: Developing high-quality visualizations and data products that return insights directly to the folks on the water.




Background
I started at NOAA Fisheries in workign at the Northeast Fisheries Science Center collaboration with SMAST UMASS Dartmouth as a CINAR postdoctoral fellow looking at the oceanographic drivers of the Northern Shortfin Squid (Illex illecebrosus). Knowing very little about the squid fishery in the Northwest Atlantic, necessitated that I talk with commercial squid fishermen in our region. I also had a lot to learn about the underlying mechanisms in our extremely dynamic ocean, connecting me with local oceanographers. Through this opportunity to listen and learn from this amazing group of folks, I quickly developed a deep passion and respect for Cooperative Research.
I have since expanded my research portfolio to include a few other commercially important species including:

Longfin Squid(Doryteuthis pealeii)https://www.fisheries.noaa.gov/species/longfin-squid
Golden Tilefish (Lopholatilus chamaeleonticeps)


Prior to working in the fisheries world, I was modeling metacommunity dynamics to understand the interplay of abiotic and biotic drivers in marine ecosystems. I used mathematical models, computer simulations and statistical analyses to explore potential vulnerabilities of ecoystems in an era of global change. You can read more about that research here.
